name: Introduction and overview — SR-71 Blackbird — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — SR-71 Blackbird
description: Introduction and overview of the SR-71 Blackbird: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The SR-71 Blackbird is a twin-engine Mach 3+ strategic reconnaissance aircraft built by Lockheed's Skunk Works, entering service in 1966. Flying above 85,000 feet at over 2,100 mph, it outran every missile fired at it — none was ever shot down. 32 were built; the type was retired in 1998 and still holds speed and altitude records. Baseline facts: Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft; service 1966-1998; 32 built by Lockheed Skunk Works; never shot down..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: SR-71 Blackbird: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft; service 1966-1998; 32 built by Lockheed Skunk Works; never shot down.
Key figure: Mach 3.3+ at 85,000+ ft; two Pratt & Whitney J58 turbojets; titanium airframe.

description: Maintenance and operations of the SR-71 Blackbird: What it takes to keep this aircraft flying: inspections, spares, and support. The SR-71 Blackbird is a twin-engine Mach 3+ strategic reconnaissance aircraft built by Lockheed's Skunk Works, entering service in 1966. Flying above 85,000 feet at over 2,100 mph, it outran every missile fired at it — none was ever shot down. 32 were built; the type was retired in 1998 and still holds speed and altitude records. Baseline facts: Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft; service 1966-1998; 32 built by Lockheed Skunk Works; never shot down..
